slides.title:
Age 52. He sold
milkshake machines.
Then *a burger stand*
changed his life.
slides.sub:
How Ray Kroc turned it into
McDonald's 👇

slides.title:
Ray Kroc is a traveling
salesman of *Multimixer*
milkshake machines.
slides.sub:
He had mortgaged his home to become
the machine's distributor (247 Wall St).

slides.title:
One small restaurant in
San Bernardino orders
*8 of his machines*.
slides.sub:
An unusual order. He drives out
to see why (Wikipedia,
Encyclopedia.com, 247 Wall St).

slides.title:
The McDonald brothers'
*Speedee system*: a short
menu, burgers in seconds.
slides.sub:
15-cent hamburgers since 1948.
100+ customers at lunchtime
(McDonald's, PBS SoCal).

slides.title: Visions of McDonald's restaurants dotting crossroads all over the country *paraded through my brain*.
slides.author:
Ray Kroc, Grinding It Out
(via Encyclopedia.com)

slides.title:
April 15: Kroc opens his
first McDonald's in
*Des Plaines, Illinois*.
slides.sub:
He sells franchises of the brothers'
system across America
(McDonald's, EBSCO).

slides.title:
In 1961, the salesman
*buys out* the
McDonald brothers.
slides.sub:
$2.7 million (McDonald's, UNH).
By his death in 1984: about 7,500
restaurants (Wikipedia).

slides.title:
Don't just sell.
*Build a system*.
slides.sub:
Kroc didn't invent the burger.
He made the experience fast and
the same every time.

✅ A short, clear catalog
✅ A checkout in a few taps
✅ Delivery times you always keep
✅ The same experience for every buyer
